deals.travelWindow: Nov 7 – Dec 13, cheapest one-way legs $56 each way
deals.whyRanked: Allegiant's calendar still shows $56 one-way legs on Nov 7, Nov 14 and Dec 13 — pairing two of those keeps Knoxville the cheapest fare of the week again, with the Smokies still 45 minutes away.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's compact grid is easy to explore alone on foot, and the Cosby and Greenbrier entrances to the Smokies are a short solo drive with none of the Cades Cove crowds.

highlights: World's Fair Park and the Sunsphere
Market Square farmers' stalls and street music
Knoxville Botanical Garden's 47 acres of trails
South Knoxville's urban wilderness bike/hike trails
Cosby entrance to the Great Smoky Mountains
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, walk World's Fair Park up to the Sunsphere deck for sunset, then dinner on Market Square.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Cosby: Hen Wallow Falls trail, Foothills Parkway overlooks on the way back.
Day 3 — Morning loop on South Knoxville's urban wilderness trails, Knoxville Botanical Garden before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is walkable end to end; a rental car is required to reach the national park entrances.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near Market Square or Gay Street — walkable to restaurants and the Tennessee Theatre.

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's fare calendar still confirms $59 one-ways on Oct 21, 22, 24, 26, 28 and 29 — tied with Baltimore at the $118 floor, and the Metro plus free Smithsonians keep DC's solo score highest of the five.
deals.soloWhy: The Metro reaches nearly every monument and museum, the Mall is safe to walk solo well into the evening, and the Smithsonians are free.

highlights: Tidal Basin loop past the Jefferson Memorial
Eastern Market on a weekend morning
Great Falls Park overlook on the Potomac
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, drop bags, Tidal Basin loop at golden hour, dinner near Eastern Market.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Shenandoah: Skyline Drive to Hawksbill summit, back for an H Street dinner.
Day 3 — Great Falls Park towpath walk in the morning, a Smithsonian of choice before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Metro covers the Mall, museums, and most neighborhoods; a rental car is only needed for Shenandoah or Great Falls.
guide.stayArea: Near a Metro stop on the Orange/Blue/Silver line (Capitol Hill or Foggy Bottom) for the fastest reach to the Mall.

deals.travelWindow: Oct 22 – Jan 6, cheapest late-Oct and mid-Nov pairings
deals.whyRanked: Southwest's calendar confirms $59 one-ways on Oct 22, 27–28, Nov 17–19, Dec 12 and even Jan 6 — tied with DC for cheapest, but Assateague's 2.5-hour drive and a lower solo score keep it third.
deals.soloWhy: The Inner Harbor and Fells Point are flat, walkable, and full of counter-seating spots that make solo dining easy, with a water taxi linking the neighborhoods.

itinerary: Day 1 — Inner Harbor on arrival, National Aquarium, water taxi to Fells Point for oysters at a counter stool.
Day 2 — Fort McHenry in the morning, Federal Hill Park for the skyline view, dinner in Fells Point.
Day 3 — Baltimore Museum of Art, Lexington Market crab cakes before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Inner Harbor, Fells Point, and Fort McHenry are covered by the water taxi and a short walk or rideshare; no rental car needed unless heading to Assateague.
guide.stayArea: Fells Point or the Inner Harbor — walkable, close to the water taxi and restaurants.

deals.whyRanked: Allegiant prices one-way legs at $79 on Oct 24 and JetBlue matches around $80 on Oct 24/27 — the cheapest fare available past the top 3 this week, with the Everglades under an hour away.
deals.soloWhy: The free Sun Trolley links the beach and Las Olas without a car, and the beachfront promenade stays lively and well-lit well into the evening for solo walks.

highlights: Wilton Manors' Hagen Park farmers market
itinerary: Day 1 — Check in near the beach, promenade walk at sunset, Las Olas for dinner and people-watching.
Day 2 — Drive to Shark Valley for the flat 15-mile Everglades bike loop, alligators sunning along the canal, back for a sunset canal cruise.
Day 3 — Bonnet House gardens in the morning, Wilton Manors for lunch before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free Sun Trolley covers downtown, Las Olas, and the beach; a rental car is worth it only for the Everglades day trip.
guide.stayArea: The beachfront or Las Olas — both walkable to restaurants, the promenade, and water taxi stops.

deals.whyRanked: Southwest's calendar confirms $100 one-ways on Oct 21 and Oct 27 — pairing those is a $200 round trip, still the priciest of the five, but Nashville's fares held near $148–$164 one-way and Denver's round trip still runs about $218, leaving Tampa's free water taxi as the better solo value at #5.
deals.soloWhy: The Tampa Riverwalk and free Pirate Water Taxi link downtown, Ybor City, and the Channel District, so a solo traveler can cover most of the city's highlights without renting a car.

highlights: Ybor City's cigar-factory history and nightlife
itinerary: Day 1 — Riverwalk stroll from Curtis Hixon Park to the Florida Aquarium, sunset drinks at a Channelside rooftop.
Day 2 — Pirate Water Taxi to Ybor City for a cigar-factory walking tour and Cuban sandwich lunch, evening back downtown.
Day 3 — Tampa Museum of Art in the morning, Bern's Steak House dinner before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free Pirate Water Taxi and TECO streetcar cover downtown, the Channel District, and Ybor City; a rental car isn't necessary for a short trip.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near the Riverwalk or the Channel District — walkable to the water taxi and Amalie Arena.
